findings.claim: CheckPolicy trusts the working-tree policy's Mode when base resolution fails, so a single working-tree edit setting {"mode":"free","base_ref":"does-not-exist"} makes gated/strict enforcement silently return clean instead of the hard error the README guarantees.
findings.fix: Do not let the baseErr branch trust the working policy's Mode: either make policyBase always fall back to the default candidate list (origin/HEAD, origin/main, main, master) even when policy.BaseRef is set, or distinguish a missing policy.json (legitimate free bootstrap) from an existing file that claims free — the latter with an unresolvable base must be a hard error; add a regression test combining a bad base_ref with mode free over a gated base.

findings.claim: The new skill-invoke-gate.sh PreToolUse enforcement hook and its test have no corresponding plan entry under plans/v1-2-1/, so this second security-relevant hook's design cannot be traced to an approved decision.
findings.fix: Confirm the hook was deliberately scoped under a plan (possibly outside plans/v1-2-1/, e.g. the skillroutine-eval single-pass fanout work) rather than added ad hoc, and document the design decision.

findings.claim: buildBinaries always rebuilds verifier binaries via go build unless a prebuilt exists at srcDir, so every Dist invocation pays a full go build per verifier with no caching.
findings.fix: Worth flagging only if Dist ever runs on a hot path; it currently doesn't (manual/CI-adjacent operation).

findings.claim: The hook's Bash context-dir read denial only matches an exact two-argument cat invocation and disables itself on any shell metacharacter, so it documents intent rather than enforcing a boundary.
findings.fix: Make the hook's comment explicit that the Bash check is advisory-only, not a real boundary, so nobody later treats it as one in the policy engine's authoritative/advisory split.

findings.claim: handleReposAdd treats any stat failure on .git as needs-init (gitErr != nil rather than os.IsNotExist), so a transient stat error triggers a redundant git init -b main on an already-initialized repo.
findings.fix: Add a one-line comment noting the intentional gitErr != nil treats any stat failure as needs-init, not just os.IsNotExist.
